title: Typed AST validator and staged migration for routing config DSL
creator: Maya Kapoor
description: Refactor the routing policy validator to first compile the DSL to a typed AST, run a contextual linter with precise error locations and fix suggestions, and provide a staged config migration path for deprecated rule patterns. Goal is safer, faster validation with actionable errors for PMs and SREs, while enabling automated upgrades for common legacy config shapes.
acceptance_criteria: DSL parsing produces a typed AST with source spans for every node
Schema validator surfaces contextual errors (eg: incompatible model variant fallback + region constraint) with actionable suggestions
A migration runner can transform at least three legacy patterns into new canonical forms and produces a dry-run diff
CI gate runs the validator and linter on all PRs modifying /policies and fails on high-severity linter errors
Runtime validators cache compiled policy artifacts and validate within SLO (validation < 50ms for 95th percentile on CI hardware)
notes_and_work_log: 2026-02-15 - Ticket created after infra spike where ambiguous errors caused config rollout rollback. Linked notes in Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/RoutingPolicy/TypedAST-Notes
2026-02-18 - Proto design: typed nodes include RegionConstraint, TierSelector, ModelVariantSet, FallbackChain. Chosen to keep AST narrow and explicit to make semantic checks easier.

2026-02-25 - Trade-offs discussed with runtime team: validating full semantics in CI vs. lightweight pre-commit check. Decided on two-phase: fast schema + linter in pre-commit, deep semantic check in CI that can reference model inventory.

2026-03-02 - Implemented AST with source spans and initial linter rule: detect mutually exclusive region+tier constraints. Found 12 historical config files that would have been blocked; added migration transforms for 8 patterns.
2026-03-05 - PR opened: github.com/redwood-inference/policy-engine/pull/374 - initial typed AST + basic linter rules. Requesting eng review from @rafael and @tess
2026-03-08 - Perf note: initial compiler added 18ms median validation time; added caching layer to reduce repeated compile cost. Need perf regression test in CI.
2026-03-10 - Design review with PM/Product: include a dry-run migration endpoint in console and present diff with suggested accept/rollback. UX ticket to design team created: DES-284
Next steps: expand linter rules to cover fallback-variant compatibility matrix, add integration test against model catalog, wire up canary rollout for automated migration (opt-in).
review_feedback: PM (Ravi Patel) - requested clearer severity levels for linter rules and a mapping to rollback behavior in console
Design (Tess Nguyen) - wants diff UX and an option to preview migrated traffic routing for a single route in the Console
Security (Anika Rao) - asked to confirm migration runner does not alter any KMS or secret references and to include audit log entries for automated migrations
implementation_plan: 1) Build typed AST with parser that emits source spans and raw token context
2) Implement core linter rules: exclusivity checks, region-model compatibility, tier fallback validation
3) Add migration transformer library with dry-run mode producing unified diffs
4) Expose validator + migration endpoints used by CI and by Console dry-run UX
5) Add caching + validation SLO tests in CI, and performance benchmarks
6) Roll out canary on 10% of policy rollouts and measure false-positive rate before full-enforcement
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Validator false-positives block legitimate configs. Mitigation: start with warnings and opt-in canary enforcement; provide --allowlist for trusted routes
Risk: Migration transforms could semantically change routing. Mitigation: dry-run with diffs + manual approval; keep migration idempotent and reversible
Risk: Validation latency impacts CI throughput. Mitigation: cache compiled artifacts and run deep checks only in CI, not on local pre-commit unless asked
